fix.shows: Deccan Herald sets the draft rolls of the special summary revision in 13 states and union territories against the final rolls of the intensive revision, and of Assam's special revision, and reports that their rolls grew from 45.22 crore to 45.96 crore. It says these states and union territories held 49.61 crore electors before the intensive revision. It gives the largest rise in numbers to Uttar Pradesh, 18.84 lakh or 1.4%, from 13.39 crore to 13.58 crore, and puts Bihar next, with its roll rising from 7.42 crore to 7.55 crore. It gives Rajasthan 11.47 lakh or 2.23%, Tamil Nadu 10.39 lakh or 1.83%, Kerala 4.06 lakh or 1.51%, Chhattisgarh 2.85 lakh or 1.53%, Assam 2.18 lakh or 0.88%, Uttarakhand 1.19 lakh or 1.66%, Manipur 33,737 or 1.72%, Puducherry 12,786 or 1.35% and Lakshadweep 94 or 0.16%. It puts the largest rise in proportion in Goa, 3.01%, from 10.57 lakh to 10.89 lakh. It reports that drafts had been published in 15 states, with no data for Punjab and Gujarat, and that the summary revision was announced in Karnataka and Meghalaya on 16 November. It reports that the Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised concerns over the delay in holding the summary revision in states where the intensive revision had finished. It reports that parties will now be given the draft and final rolls free of cost as readable PDFs without photographs of the electors, along with a physical copy, and that the Commission had earlier refused machine-readable rolls.

note: Second reading, 18 November 2026, of the Deccan Herald page fetched again with curl and read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody (isAccessibleForFree true). Headline, the byline Shemin Joy, the dateline New Delhi and datePublished 2026-11-17T21:11:34+05:30 match. Both quotes are verbatim. Every figure was checked again against the article and against data/india/raw/ssr_draft.csv, final.csv and states.csv. The first reader's agreements stand: Uttar Pradesh 18,84,113 (1.41%), Rajasthan 11,47,487 (2.23%), Tamil Nadu 10,39,238 (1.83%), Kerala 4,06,610 (1.51%), Chhattisgarh 2,85,854 (1.53%, which the paper gives as 2.85 lakh), Uttarakhand 1,19,086 (1.66%), Manipur 33,737 (1.72%), Puducherry 12,786 (1.35%), Lakshadweep 94 (0.16%), and Assam's net rise of 2,18,771 (4,12,344 added less 1,93,573 deleted, 0.88% of 2,49,58,139). Bihar's roll from 7.42 crore to 7.55 crore and Tamil Nadu's from 5.67 crore to 5.77 crore agree. The first reader's four disagreements stand. Goa is printed as an increase of 31,185, where the file has 31,815 (10,89,381 against 10,57,566), and the paper's own 10.57 lakh, 10.89 lakh and 3.01% agree with 31,815. Madhya Pradesh is printed as 8.90 lakh or 1.65%, where the file has 8,18,563 or 1.52%. Bihar is printed as 13.89 lakh or 1.87%, where the file has 13,97,008 or 1.88%. The site's figures for the 13 add to 73,95,162 more, from 45,22,07,173 to 45,96,02,335, or 1.64%, and the paper's 74.66 lakh and 1.65% are 70,838 higher, about the 71,437 by which its Madhya Pradesh figure exceeds the file. Corrected: the summary carried the paper's 74.66 lakh and 1.65%, which do not agree with the rolls it sets side by side, and it now gives only the 45.22 crore and 45.96 crore, which do. It said all 13 were set against the final rolls of the intensive revision, and the paper says Assam's earlier roll came from a special revision, so the summary now says so. It said parties are given readable rolls after the Commission refused machine-readable ones, and the paper gives the refusal as earlier history and no sequence, so the summary now says earlier. Not carried, as in the first reading: the paper's 5.15 crore to 5.26 crore for Rajasthan (the file's draft is 5,26,67,416, which is 5.27 crore when rounded) and its account of claims about voters turning 18. The 49.61 crore before the intensive revision is carried as the paper's and cannot be checked, because the site holds no roll for Assam before its special revision.
